Subject: Hosted API latency SLOs during migration - request for temporary measurement-window amendment

Hi Rishi / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinOptics is moving quickly and we have a major data migration planned for the week of Nov 9 that will briefly amplify inference traffic and tail latency while we warm caches and run batch re-ingest. Our legal/procurement team is asking for a short-term, narrowly scoped amendment to the hosted API SLO language to avoid a technical breach during that period.

Specific ask: allow a temporary, time-boxed modification of the p95 measurement policy for the hosted text-generation route used by FinOptics so that (a) we can apply a 10-day grace window during migration where failures and sustained tail spikes are carved out for the p95 calculation, or alternatively (b) an agreed temporary p95 threshold increase (e.g. 700ms → 1200ms) for the migration window.

We need the amendment language and an evidence checklist for audits (NOC reports, traffic charts, canary results) by Oct 6 so procurement can draft the contract addendum. Please also indicate whether this change requires any config-level coordination (routing, canary tags, or reassigning to dedicated capacity) on your side.

Cc'ing our procurement contact.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, FinOptics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLOs during migration - request for temporary measurement-window amendment

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the timeline. We can support a temporary, narrowly scoped accommodation for customers undergoing planned platform maintenance/migration, but we need to settle the exact mechanics so the language is actionable for both sides and instrumentable for audits.

Quick clarifications and our proposed approach:
1) Measurement model options (choose one):
   - Rolling-window carveout: exclude a contiguous N-day slice from the p95 computation (we suggest 10 days). This requires you to notify us 7 days in advance and provide the migration start/end window. We will tag affected traffic and exclude it from the rolling p95 for contract audits.
   - Temporary threshold increase: a time-boxed increase to the committed p95 threshold for the named route for the migration window. This keeps measurement intact but relaxes the numeric target.

2) Evidence & guardrails we require:
   - Migration runbook and calendar (to validate dates).
   - Canary pass/fail logs (we require canary to hit production traffic for ≥4 hours without critical errors before extending the carveout).
   - NOC incident log export and request ID for any spike events during the window.
   - Post-migration summary within 5 business days with token-level latency percentiles and a sample of failing requests.

3) Config coordination: tagging is simple on our side — we add a temporary customer traffic tag to the measurement pipeline. No dedicated capacity is required for the carveout, but if you want absolute throughput isolation we can discuss a short dedicated pool (will require a capacity commit).

4) Draft amendment language (high level):
   - "For the period Nov 9, 2026 through Nov 19, 2026, the p95 latency commitment for Customer's hosted API route will be adjusted as follows: [either carveout of 10 contiguous days from the rolling p95 calculation OR an adjusted p95 numeric target of 1200ms for the named route]. Either option requires Customer to submit migration schedule and supporting evidence per Exhibit A. Redwood shall tag traffic and provide measurement exports for the amended window on request."

I attached an SLO evidence checklist template to speed procurement review (slo-evidence-template.xlsx).

Next steps: please confirm which measurement option you prefer and share the migration runbook. I'll draft precise amendment wording and loop in legal if needed. Cc'ing Kim to make sure this aligns with our SLA and billing teams.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — looping procurement for visibility.
Elena
